name: Source Comparison
description: The mastered value and every contributing source's value for one record, side by side — one row per field, one column per source, with the winning contribution marked and disagreements flagged.

generation.purpose: Answer 'where did this value come from and does anything disagree with it' for one record, by pivoting long-form contribution rows into a field-by-source matrix.
generation.whenToUse: On a detail page for a single mastered record, bound to a data source that returns LONG form — one row per (field, contributing source) — such as `securities.source-value` filtered to one security and NOT filtered by source. Bind `field` (becomes a row), `source` (becomes a column, in query order) and `value` (the cell) at minimum. Bind `current` as well and the mastered value leads the matrix, which is what makes it §28’s side-by-side comparison rather than a survey of vendors — and it is what makes "every source agrees but the mastered value differs" detectable, which is the case a steward most needs. `winner` marks the contribution that won, `agreement` carries the source’s own match code, `confidence` shows a score per cell.
generation.whenNotToUse: Do not use for a list of records: it shows one record's provenance and has no row per entity. Do not use it as a general grid over the same entity — `data.table` is right when the reader wants to scan or sort the raw contributions. Do not use it for an aggregate such as 'disagreements by source'; that is `analytics.chart`.

emphasiseDisagreements.description: Mark fields whose sources do not agree with each other, or with the mastered value. On by default: a comparison that does not point at the disagreements leaves the reader to perform the comparison themselves.

disagreementsOnly.description: Start with only the disagreeing fields shown. Off by default, because the whole record is the context a steward reads a disagreement against.

showConfidence.description: Show each contribution's confidence score in its cell. Requires the `confidence` role to be bound.

currentLabel.description: What to call the mastered value. "Current" is the PRD's word; a tenant may say "Golden" or "Published".

maxHeight.description: Scroll the matrix body beyond this height, keeping the source names visible.

contributionActivated.label: Contribution activated
contributionActivated.description: Emitted when one source's cell is clicked or activated with Enter. Payload carries the field, the source, the value and the underlying row. It resolves nothing — choosing which source should win is a stewardship action the page binds.

xs.note: The matrix scrolls sideways with the field name pinned. It deliberately does NOT stack: stacking a pivot destroys the one property it exists for, which is that values in a column are comparable at a glance.

accessibility.keyboardContract: The matrix is a table. Tab moves between contribution cells, Enter activates the focused cell. The field column and the source header are real `th` elements with scope, so a screen reader announces both coordinates of a cell.
accessibility.notes: A disagreeing row carries the words "sources differ" as well as an emphasis background, and a winning contribution carries the word "mastered" as well as weight — a coloured row is never the only signal. A source that supplied nothing reads "not supplied" rather than being an empty cell, which is a distinction assistive technology would otherwise lose entirely.
